segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakashwani. I am Valsa Williams with the news at 9.
The headlines. Home Minister Amit Shah says drug menace burdens economy and funds anti-national

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has termed drug abuse a major challenge to the nation.
He said the menace threatens future generations, places an undue burden on the economy and
provides financial support to organizations involved in anti-national activities.
Mr. Shah called upon police forces across the country to work collectively towards
was eradicating the threat of narcotics by 2029. He was addressing the police commemoration
day ceremony at the National Police Memorial in New Delhi today.
Drugs are a serious menace that weaken our youth, undermine our economic system and provide
support to anti-national organizations. Our Honourable Prime Minister, Srinarendra Modi
ji, has vowed to eradicate the menace of drugs and today I call upon all police
personnel to stand united and resolve to fulfill this mission and protect the future of our
next generation.
The Central Bureau of Investigation, CBI, has taken over the probe into the killing of
Mansa-based anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh in Punjab.
A team led by a senior Deputy Inspector General-level officer will examine the case
with all the facts and figures.
The development comes hours after Union Home Minister Amit Shah assured Parvinder
Singh's family of a CBI probe during his visit to Punjab.
The anti-drug activist was shot dead in Mansaf for confronting a chemist over alleged synthetic
drug sales.
The Ministry of Defence has signed a contract with Bharat Electronic Limited to procure
improved low-level lightweight radar LLRI at a cost of nearly 770 crore rupees for
the army capable to detect micro drones.
The contract was signed in New Delhi today in the presence of Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh.
We have more from our correspondent.
The radar system is capable of detecting and tracking fighter-sized targets as well as mini and micro drones.
It has also the capability of prioritizing aerial targets.
This will enable the Army to successfully counter the threat of unmanned aerial system.
Aligning with the government's vision of Vixit Bharat 2047,
the procurement is a significant step towards indigenization of air defense platforms.
This will boost India's defence manufacturing ecosystem, including micro, small and medium
enterprises, and help build a resilient, self-reliant and globally competitive defence
industry.
Anand Kumar, Akashwani News, Delhi.
The bi-annual Army Commanders Conference commenced in New Delhi today.
The three-day conference being chaired by the Chief of the Army's staff, General
Dheeraj Seth, brings together the Army's senior leadership to discuss the evolving
security environment, operational preparedness, capability development, and the modernization
of the force. Defense Minister Rajnath Singh will address the conference on Friday.
India and New Zealand have signed a memorandum of cooperation for the electronic exchange of
trade-related origin data aimed at deepening customs cooperation, facilitating bilateral trade,
and helping businesses access tariff benefits under the recently implemented
free trade agreement FTA between the two countries.
The New Zealand FTA came into force yesterday, opening new opportunities for exporters and
businesses in both countries.
We have a report.
The memorandum of cooperation between the two countries will deepen customs cooperation
and support the effective implementation of trade facilitation measures.
The initiative reflects a forward-looking approach to align bilateral customs cooperation
with evolving international practices in digitalisation, information exchange and trade
facilitation. The electronic exchange of origin data is expected to improve operational
efficiency, reduce information gaps and provide greater certainty to traders engaged in bilateral
trade. The arrangement will support the effective utilisation of trade preferences under the
India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement.
Supranasekya, Aakashwani News, Delhi.
Prime Minister of Poland, Donald Tusk will arrive in New Delhi tonight on a three-day
visit to India.
Mr. Tusk will hold bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi tomorrow, during which
both leaders shall review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News.

New and Renewable Energy Minister Pranlalad Joshi today said, India is the only country
which has performed well economically amid the situation of unrest globally. Mr Joshi
was addressing the inaugural ceremony of the three-day AgriVoltaics World Conference
in New Delhi.
Lot of developments are happening in India.
One is overall growth in the economy which we have seen 7.8 percent growth in the first
quarter.
When the world is really under the crisis, India is the only country which has performed
so well as far as economy is concerned.
Even today we are the fastest growing economy of the world.

Speaking at the event, Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan said
Agrivol takes offers a promising path towards global welfare by enabling farmers to grow
crops while generating solar power on the same land.
This is a remarkable model that combines farming with electricity generation, allowing
farmers to cultivate their land while producing power.
The vision of making farmers energy providers will no longer remain merely a slogan, it
will become a reality.
I wholeheartedly welcome this initiative and I show you that the Department of Agriculture
will work hand in hand with you, standing shoulder to shoulder and make every possible
effort to ensure the successful implementation of this model.
The information and broadcasting ministry has advised all private satellite TV channels
to exercise caution while using artificial intelligence AI tools in their programs and
warned against sensationalized crime reporting.
In a letter, the ministry has urged them to limit the use of AI tools for assistive
capacity without compromising the accuracy, authenticity or sensitivity of the news content
while adhering to the programme code. The Ministry also advised them that the telecast
of scenes related to crime and violence should be based on verified facts and truths, and
the reporting should be in a balanced and responsible manner. The advisory said the
Ministry can take action on the violation of the programme code under the provisions
of the Cable Television Network's Regulation Act 1995.
The Union Finance Ministry today launched a nationwide financial inclusion campaign
at the grump and jive and urban local body levels.
The campaign will run till the 31st of December this year,
covering 2,70,000 grump and jive and urban local bodies.
The initiative aims to expand access to financial services
measures, and ensure that eligible beneficiaries are covered under key government schemes.
The Commission for Air Quality Management in the National Capital Region and adjoining
areas CAQM subcommittee on the Graded Response Action Plan, GRAP, today invoked all actions
under Stage 1 of GRAP with immediate effect across the entire NCR.
The move came after Delhi's Air Quality Index was recorded 244 at 2pm today, placing
it in the poor category. BJP President Nitin Naveen today addressed the 75th Foundation Day
of the Bharatiya Jan Sangh in New Delhi commemorating the octogenarian members of the Jan Sangh who have
played a crucial role in its inception in 1951. Mr. Naveen highlighted how the party reached
303 seats from three in the first general election. You are listening to the news at 9 on
Aakashwani.

Our Kolkata correspondent has the details.
With the iconic phrase, Asche Vachur Avarhabe, meaning, Ma Durga will return again next
year, Bengalis are bidding farewell to the goddess.
Today is Vijay Dasami, the culmination of Durga Puja Festival in Bengal.
With heavy hearts and tears in their eyes, the immersion of Ma Durga idols is taking
place across the state.
processions carrying the Durga idols have been arranged leading up to the Ghats.
People are exchanging greetings and sweets, while youngsters show respect to
elders by touching their feet.
In Bangladesh, devotees observed the occasion with religious fervor while
married women participated in the traditional Shindur Khalla ritual.
Meanwhile, the world-famous Mysuru Dasara festivities in Karnataka culminated today.
Renowned master craftsmen and veteran juror Thiru Vumidi Aithiraj, who played a crucial
role in the making of India's historic Senkhol, passed away in 10 day today at the age of 99.
The President, Vice President and Prime Minister have expressed grief at the demise of the
eminent artisan, remembering his role in crafting the iconic Senkhol.
Under sports Indian Varra at least delivered impressive performances across track and field
events on the third day of the Asian Paragames in Aichi, Nakoya, Japan, taking the country's
overall medal tally past the 60 mark.
India clinched 27 medals today, including five gold, 11 silver and 11 bronze.
With this, the country's overall medal tally has reached 62, comprising 14 gold, 22 silver
and 26 bronze medals.
India has currently placed fifth in the overall standings.
Dilip Gavit won a gold medal in the men's 100-metre T46-47 combined event in the men's
short put F46 event such as J. R. R. Khilary bagged gold Aayush Verma won gold in the men's
short put F53 event while Praveen Kumar won gold in the men's high jump T44-64 event.
Sprinter Simran won gold in the women's 100-metre T12 event.
The President, Vice President and Prime Minister have extended wishes to the medal winners.
